entities.text: BABLU Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADES
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Notice has been served to the victim and State has filed the reply.

Learned Trial Court has convicted the appellant under Sections 366 of IPC and 376(3) of the IPC and sentenced him to undergo RI for 5 years with fine of Rs.1000/- and RI for 20 years with fine of Rs.10,000, respectively with default stipulations vide judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 15.03.2023 passed by the Special Judge, (POCSO) Act, Mandleshwar, West Nimar, (MP) in Special Session Case No.
265/2019.
Prosecution story found to be proved is that the prosecutrix resides with her grandmother.
On 24.04.2019 at around 04:00 PM she left her house informing her grandmother that she is going to the house of her maternal uncle.
But when she not returned home, family members inquired from their relatives of her presence at their house and maternal uncle told them that the prosecutrix not visited his home.
On the pretext of absconding with the appellant, a crime has been registered against the appellant accused.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence and he has been falsely implicated in the case.
There are no chance of accused being absconded.
In this case trial Court has wrongly ascertained the age of the prosecutirx and she has not supported the prosecution case and she was the consenting party.
The appellant is in custody since the date of his arrest.
Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence may be suspended and the appellant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and submitted that the prosecutrix is not the consenting party and she was minor during the time of incident i.e only 14 years and 8 months.
Moreso, appellant has not suffered considerable period of custody.
Hence, the application for suspension deserves to be dismissed.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
In this case, looking to the tender age of the appellant, we deem it fit to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant Bablu S/o Dayaram Dawar. .

9. Accordingly, I.A. No. 9929/2023 is allowed and it is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty thousand Only) with solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 10.09.2024 and on such subsequent dates as may be fixed in this regard, sentence of imprisonment awarded to him shall remain suspended till further orders and he shall be released on bail.
List this matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(S. A. DHARMADHIKARI) (DEVNARAYAN MISHRA)
 JUDGE JUDGE  rashmi Bablu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19285896/
